[] kitsuned wow, does HDMI CEC can really adjust audio sync?
.kriilunaus 02/26/2024 5:51 PM
HDMI CEC doesn't adjust audio sync. In a proper HDMI device chain, each
HDMI device implementing the standard reports the value of additional
audio and video processing delay caused by the device and its settings.
A TV at the end of the chain therefore receives the total delay values
of the entire signal chain and can act accordingly. The corresponding
information is communicated via HDMI CEC. The HDMI specification
describes this "Auto Lipsync Correction Feature" in the corresponding
specification documents.
[jaruba]
jaruba 02/26/2024 5:51 PM
@hellobox i think i may be missing too many details of the discussions,
what is umediaserver in this case? do we need to root the device to
access such logs?
hellobox. 02/26/2024 5:48 PM
@jaruba have you looked in the logs? umediaserver seems to log a bunch
of stuff in uMediaServer::uMediaserver::selectTrackCommand
[] pinheadi if I use the av sync it's working if i wanna make the delay
bigger  i.e more than 0, I want to be ...
.kriilunaus 02/26/2024 5:44 PM
If you need a negative audio delay then this usually means that you have
a problem with the source and not with the devices / TV. That's because
each device in your chain adds some extra delay due to its A/V
processing. I.e. there's actually no such thing as a negative audio
delay in the signal chain. And that's also why you can't set a negative
value in the settings. If you say that you do not have the problems with
another device chain, then it cannot be ruled out that one of the
devices is behaving incorrectly and delivering incorrect delay values.
With some video players, however, you can make finer A/V synchronization
settings (negative audio delay values) to correct problems with the
source. These settings may also help you achieve your goal.
